sights.w: A landmark 1836-37 National Road stagecoach inn in tiny Lafayette, said to be second only to the Golden Lamb among Ohio's oldest continuously recognized taverns; it hosted six U.S. presidents. Documented by the Library of Congress HABS survey. Closed 2020, reopened Feb 2023 and still operating as a historic tavern you can walk into.

The county historical society's museum in downtown London, with local-history galleries and a relocated one-room schoolhouse (Beach School) on the grounds. A quiet hidden gem on the courthouse-square side of town.

sights.address: 3225 Plain City-Georgesville Rd, West Jefferson, OH 43162
sights.w: A 2,200-acre Metro Park straddling the Madison-Franklin line along Big Darby Creek (a state and national scenic river), with restored prairie, quarry-pond beaches and paddling, and prime birding. The Madison County side lies west of the creek. Distinct from Battelle Darby Creek downstream.
